title: Record the characteristic polynomial of one 216-dimensional A1 joint eigenspace
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Finite exact characteristic polynomial, over `Q`, of one explicit 216-dimensional joint eigenspace of the historical one-slot operator `A_1`. The space is the joint `(+1,+1)` eigenspace of the `c=1` sign stabilizer and the involutions `g` and `t`. The basis, the integer matrix of `B = 4 A_1`, and the monic polynomial are pinned. The same polynomial is the characteristic polynomial on each of the four joint sign spaces.

No new kappa. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`. This polynomial does not replace the degree-881 one-slot minimal polynomial. It locates one invariant subspace inside that certificate.

Because `x` and `x - 2` both divide the polynomial, this 216-dimensional space has a proper nonzero `A_1`-invariant rational subspace. The package does not construct that subspace and does not search a centralizer. Eigenvalue `0` has algebraic multiplicity 24. The geometric multiplicity is not computed.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed.
- Upstream base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` (priority revision 8). This fork draft is based on that pin. It is not an upstream pull request.
- Handoff: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19144258

- Live query: `research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/frozen/work/centre-encoding-campaign-20261014/lanes/circuit-interface/INTERFACE.json`, SHA256 `5c6c51fbffc07a683e922f17532fd90262ae9e23cc3560a696002073dd234ef3`, git blob `4201e9a04c12273b919e2cae60a6b6482c8150f3`.

The catalogue card asks for a formal caller binding. The handoff asks for a decomposition of the largest sign-character space of the `c=1` centre block. The sign-stabilizer split, fork draft https://github.com/unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds/pull/153 at `26ceb7a0b4e04d4377a31aaa849dcb13e06e4cbc`, constructed the dimension 216 and left this polynomial uncomputed. This package answers that polynomial for one explicit joint eigenspace. It does not add a Lean binding.

Related packages on the same Gram, with different claims:

- `research/centre-sign-stabilizer-split/` (fork PR 153): dimension split, no 216-by-216 matrix.
- `research/centre-gram-degree410/` (PR5120): degree at least 410.
- `research/exact-one-slot-gram/` (PR5168): exact one-slot degree 881.
- `research/uniform-centre-gram-annihilator/`: one annihilator of degree at most `2^93` at every positive width.
- `research/equal-bell-two-slot-spectrum/` (PR5382): a different operator.

Overlap search on 2026-11-10 against upstream `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`: local notes 8917 of 8917 HEAD paths, complete; 885 open PRs, pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T02:07:47Z; 6934 discussion records, pagination complete, fetched 2026-11-10T02:08:41Z. The phrases `216-dimensional` and `216-by-216` matched nothing. `degree-881` matched the sign-stabilizer finding, which records the dimension and does not compute this polynomial, and `research/equal-bell-two-slot-spectrum/`. No open upstream PR computes this characteristic polynomial. Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, TASK metadata, and the ledger, not through code diffs.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/a1-joint-216-charpoly/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/a1-joint-216-charpoly/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a1-joint-216-charpoly --check-only
```

Marker: `PASS_A1_JOINT_216_CHARPOLY`. The registered package runner passed both commands and returned `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Metadata check returned `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Selected baseline returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

The basis is the least-index signed orbit basis of the joint `+1` equations, pinned in `research/a1-joint-216-charpoly/evidence/basis.json`. Support sizes are 1, 4, 8, and 16. The integer matrix of `B` is pinned in `research/a1-joint-216-charpoly/evidence/matrix.json`: 216 by 216, entries in `-28..28`, 3972 nonzero entries. The matrix of `A_1` is that matrix divided by 4.

Ascending-coefficient SHA256:

```text
chi_A  18114a297071c454cb935ef85cab42a745954fb065be2a6d7e4ff23ef26b771b
chi_B  ec79276843b69dc6e064cdcb009a238e8231d0a8bf8f9c532c679c6a0cb6a81e
```

`chi_A(x) = 4^{-216} chi_B(4x)`. Both are monic of degree 216 in `Z[x]`, and both are even. The irreducible factorization is copied in `research/a1-joint-216-charpoly/PROOF.md`. It begins `x^24 (x-2)^12 (x+2)^12 (x-6)^2 (x+6)^2 (x^2-2x-4) (x^2+2x-4)` and continues with paired factors of degrees 11, 14, and 16. Every irreducible factor of `chi_B` divides at least one published `c=1` sector minimal polynomial. That comparison reads coefficients. It does not replay the degree-881 certificate.

The characteristic polynomial is computed by the Hessenberg recurrence modulo primes whose product exceeds twice the Gershgorin binomial coefficient bound, then lifted by the Chinese remainder theorem. Determinants of `tI - M` at `t = 0,1,2,3,5` agree with that polynomial modulo the first three primes. Quadratics are irreducible because the discriminant 20 is not a square. Each higher factor is irreducible over `Z` by a Rabin test modulo one prime among the first 80 primes at or above 1009.

Rejection controls refuse a coordinate transposition, a swapped port label, omission of `g` unless the dimension is 432, a flipped stabilizer sign that still claims dimension 216, a one-entry change of `M` that preserves the polynomial modulo `1000003`, a missing factor, and a one-coordinate sign error in a linked basis vector.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, and the selected cold replay.

## Open next questions

See `research/a1-joint-216-charpoly/TASK.json`.

- Characteristic polynomial of one 8-dimensional joint eigenspace inside the unique 32-dimensional `c=1` sign character. The trace formula gives the dimension without listing that character's signs.
- Geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 on the pinned 216-by-216 matrix. Algebraic multiplicity is 24. A modular rank is only a lower bound on the rational rank.
